claims.text: Halt's memo records physical trace evidence: three depressions 1.5 inches deep and 7 inches in diameter, and beta/gamma readings of 0.1 milliroentgens peaking in the depressions and at the centre of the triangle they formed.

The memo describes the object as 'metalic in appearance and triangular in shape, approximately two to three meters across the base and approximately two meters high' and states 'It illuminated the entire forest with a white light.'

Halt's memorandum records that on the day after the first sighting 'three depressions 1 1/2" deep and 7" in diameter were found where the object had been sighted on the ground' and that 'Beta/Gamma readings of 0.1 milliroentgens were recorded with peak reading in the three depressions and near the center of the triangle formed by the depressions.'

edges.note: The same September 1997 OASD release that produced the Halt memo produced the November 1975 Malmstrom overflight records.

edges.label: Halt authored and signed the 'Unexplained Lights' memorandum
edges.note: Halt was Deputy Base Commander of the 81st Combat Support Group and signed the memo on 13 Jan 81. The document is his; his authorship has never been disputed by the Air Force.

edges.label: Halt personally led the 28 December 1980 forest patrol
edges.note: Halt's own memo states 'Numerous individuals, including the undersigned, witnessed the activities in paragraphs 2 and 3.'

edges.label: Released to The Black Vault under DoD FOIA case 97-F-1677
edges.note: The Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense, Freedom of Information and Security Review Office released the memo in September 1997 under case 97-F-1677.

edges.label: The memo is the primary official record of the incident
edges.note: The memo is the only contemporaneous US government document describing the events; everything else in the case is witness statement or later recollection.

edges.note: A congressionally directed review of the historical record omits the best-documented physical-trace incident at a NATO nuclear-capable base, for which the Pentagon's own FOIA office has released the commander's memorandum.
